scope: Observed existing limits before the #12633 transport changes. Final headless results qualify the changed producer separately.
findings: A 32768-byte decoded take occupies 43691 unpadded base64url characters, before URL and browser fact overhead.
The CLI and shared media URL buffers refused earlier. host.send truncates facts to the module inbox cap. The development server closed an overfull header buffer.
The cache input writer marked overflow but still exposed the truncated prefix to its digest; a long shared-prefix URL could therefore share an input identity.
The server scans only the first 1023 target characters, but query data is not needed for resolving the static page. The browser retains its complete navigation URL.
The page fingerprint client has a smaller URL bound than capture; stripping only take64 permits an HTML fingerprint while retaining other query parameters.
determinism: Shots pin t=5.5, clock=0.78 and card=1. Two independent fresh launches form one planned deterministic comparison.
The short clip resets the existing Anime page clock with message 700 and -1 before fixed-step recording. At 12 fps its first frame is at 1/12 second.
PNG comparisons decode RGBA with Coax. The MP4 is independently inspected and decoded by ffprobe/ffmpeg; H264 loss is measured rather than requiring PNG byte identity.
The combined URL/eval refusal child uses this Coax probe itself as a Chrome sentinel. A marker would reveal an attempted launch; no browser runs in that negative control.
boundaries: Inspection does not qualify a deployed page or arbitrary browser URL limits.
All capture uses the existing muted headless Chrome engine; no visible window, sound, owner identity or external model call is involved.
